`tito` is the command-line tool that sets up your environment, opens each module, checks your work, and records your progress. Every command below exists in the current release; `tito --help` and `tito <group> --help` list the rest, with every option.

## Set up once

Install TinyTorch with the one-line installer on the [Quick Start](../getting-started.qmd) page, then:

```bash
tito setup           # environment, packages, and your profile
tito system health   # check that Python, the packages, and Jupyter are ready
```

`tito setup` is safe to run again. If something in the environment breaks later, rerunning it is the first thing to try.

## The module loop

Every module follows the same four commands.

```bash
tito module start 01      # first time: create the notebook, open Jupyter Lab
tito module resume 01     # later sessions: reopen it where you left off
tito module complete 01   # test, export, and record the module
tito module status        # see which modules are done and what comes next
```

`start` creates `modules/01_tensor/tensor.ipynb` from the source and opens it. It refuses to start a module whose prerequisites are not complete, and if the module is already started it suggests `resume` instead.

`complete` stops at the first step that fails:

1. the unit tests inside your notebook run;
2. your code is exported into the `tinytorch` package;
3. the module's integration tests run against that exported package;
4. the module is recorded as done.

Modules are completed in order: `complete 05` refuses to run until 04 is complete.

Three more module commands are useful along the way.

```bash
tito module test 01       # run the same tests without exporting or recording anything
tito module view 01       # open the notebook without changing its status
tito module reset 01      # replace the notebook with a fresh copy from the source
```

**`reset` discards your notebook.** It regenerates `modules/01_tensor/tensor.ipynb` from the source with every solution cleared, and removes the module from your completed list. It does not keep a copy, so save your notebook elsewhere first if you want it.

## Milestones

A milestone runs a historical experiment on the framework you built. Each one needs a set of completed modules, and `tito` checks them before it runs anything.

```bash
tito milestone list       # the six milestones and whether each is unlocked
tito milestone info 03    # what it needs and what it runs
tito milestone run 03     # run it, after checking prerequisites
tito milestone status     # which milestones you have completed
```

Some milestones have more than one script; `tito milestone run 03 --part 2` runs only the second. The [Historical Milestones](../milestones/index.qmd) pages describe each one and the results to expect.

## Where your progress lives

`tito` keeps its records in the `.tito/` folder at the root of your TinyTorch checkout:

| File | What it records |
| :--- | :--- |
| `.tito/progress.json` | Modules you have started and completed |
| `.tito/milestones.json` | Milestones you have completed |
| `.tito/config.json` | Your settings |

: Files in the `.tito/` folder. {#tbl-tito-files tbl-colwidths="[35,65]"}

Your code is not in `.tito/`. It lives in your notebooks under `modules/` and, once exported, under `tinytorch/` (e.g. `tinytorch/core/` and `tinytorch/perf/`).

To clear records without touching code, use `tito package reset`, adding `--backup` to copy `.tito/` to a timestamped `.tito_backup_<time>/` folder first:

```bash
tito package reset progress --backup     # forget module completions
tito package reset milestones --backup   # forget milestone completions
```

## Updating TinyTorch

```bash
tito system update --check   # is a newer release available?
tito system update           # install it
```

`update` snapshots your progress files, your notebooks, and your exported code to `.tito/backups/pre_update_<time>/` before it changes anything, and it leaves `modules/` and `tinytorch/` in place.

## Joining the community (optional)

```bash
tito community login    # sign in through your browser
tito community sync     # upload your progress to your profile
tito community status   # show who you are signed in as
tito community logout
```

`sync` uploads your module and milestone progress, not your code.

## Teaching and contributing

Instructors staging assignments with nbgrader should start with [For Instructors](../instructors.qmd). Contributors changing TinyTorch itself use the `tito dev` commands described in [Developer Testing](testing.qmd).

When something goes wrong, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).
